gates.label: governance rejection cases
note format
bilingual pairing
non-trivial changes carry an Agent Note (advisory)
no unresolved conflict markers in changed files
syntax-class static checks over product code (shipped + .gov/checks/ rules)
package layering: leaves, no cycles, dispatcher on top
gates.description: gov/ stays a modular monolith: leaf modules import no gov module, only declared entrypoints import the cli dispatcher, and the import graph has no cycles (scripts/import-layers.json is the tier map)

gates.label: module size within declared limits
gates.description: every gov/ and scripts/ module stays within its declared line budget (scripts/size-limits.json) — growth lands as a reviewed diff, not as a monolith (#265)

gates.label: review rubric structure
archived-notes seal
decisions table guard
task cards
CHANGELOG ↔ HIGHLIGHTS pairing
governance-plane seal (rules + gate set tamper-evidence)
ruff (pyflakes + syntax-level pycodestyle)
gates.description: the CI lint job, gate-ized: the same ruff the lint cell runs now rides the DAG, so pre-push catches what CI used to catch first (config: [tool.ruff] in pyproject.toml)

gates.label: router skill names every shipped command (rule 9's third home)
gates.description: every COMMANDS entry in gov/commands.py appears as 'gov <cmd>' in the govrail skill's stage table, or carries a reasoned exclusion in scripts/skill-coverage.json — a new command cannot ship invisible to the surface agents enumerate

gates.label: postmortem entries carry their README contract (sections, pointed guardrails)
gates.description: every docs/postmortem entry has the four README sections in one heading vocabulary, each non-empty, and a Guardrails section that names at least one pointer with every path resolving — a postmortem without a linked guardrail is a story

gates.label: recurring surprises escalated into process improvements (rule 11)
gates.description: the surprise ledger (.gov/surprises.jsonl) is loadable and one-sided-entry free, and every signature at three or more recorded surprises has a process note citing surprise:<sig> — a recurring surprise is a process defect, not bad luck

gates.label: standing docs stay within declared character ceilings
gates.description: every standing doc in scripts/doc-budgets.json stays within its character ceiling — prose grows one paragraph at a time until the reading cost is paid forever; ledgers (decisions, CHANGELOG) are deliberately unjudged

gates.label: declared persisted-format shapes change only with a chained acknowledgment record
gates.description: every schema descriptor in docs/persistence/schemas chains through the records in docs/persistence/changes to a live-digest anchor — touching a format the plane writes without acknowledging the compatibility impact is red; catalog.json (generated) must be fresh

gates.label: commit-stage lint: ruff --fix on the staged files, fixes restaged
gates.description: the commit boundary owns what the push boundary proves: staged *.py files are autofixed and restaged (partially-staged files skipped by name so unstaged work is never swallowed); red only on findings autofix cannot clear

gates.label: commit-stage derivation: derived truths regenerate, never reject
gates.description: when a staged file is an input to a derived truth (CLI surface, templates, skills, rules, rejection cases, the derivation tooling), the truths regenerate now and the outputs restage — a forgotten regeneration costs nothing instead of a red push
